identity.name: Olatech Solutions Limited
identity.industry: Telecom & Data Center Enablement & Digital Transformation Services

summary.oneLiner: Olatech transformed from a modest software services firm to a diversified tech integrator with a 35-crore order book, driven by a landmark 45-crore bundled telecom deal spanning software, hardware, AMC, and managed services — this shifts the business model from project-based to recurring revenue, with enterprise digital and Exclusion server distribution now acting as high-growth levers.

one-line thesis: Olatech transformed from a modest software services firm to a diversified tech integrator with a 35-crore order book, driven by a landmark 45-crore bundled telecom deal spanning software, hardware, AMC, and managed services — this shifts the business model from project-based to recurring revenue, with enterprise digital and Exclusion server distribution now acting as high-growth levers.
financial scorecard: revenue: 21.04 Cr (+39% YoY); EBITDA: 5.58 Cr (+27.7% YoY, margin 26.5% vs 28.9% in H1 due to low-margin hardware sales); PAT (reported): 4.24 Cr (+41% YoY); PAT (normalized): ~3.8 Cr (excluding one-time preferential allotment gain of ~0.44 Cr); order book: 35 Cr (as of Jun 2025); net debt: 2.35 Cr borrowings (up from 45L YoY, due to office purchase and inventory build-up)
guidance: revenue growth: 50 Cr+ in FY26 (2.4x FY25); margin: target 20% PAT margin; order inflow: 45 Cr order (50% to be billed in FY26); capex/commissioning: office purchase completed (Rupa Solitaire); no new capex planned beyond inventory and branch expansion
order book & pipeline: 35 Cr total (incl. 45 Cr mega order — 50% to be billed in FY26, rest over 10 years; enterprise digital: 3 Cr; software: 15 Cr+; hardware AMC: 10 Cr+; Exclusion server: 5 Cr pipeline)
segment / subsidiary detail: Hardware AMC & EMS: 15 Cr revenue (FY25), targeting 30 Cr in FY26 (30-40% growth); Software & Products: 4.5 Cr revenue (FY25), targeting 30 Cr in FY26 (driven by 45 Cr order + new AI tools); Enterprise Digital: 1.29 Cr revenue (FY25), targeting 10 Cr in FY26 (via Olatech Digital Solutions); Exclusion Server Distribution: 0 in FY25, targeting 5 Cr in FY26 (H1 start); Influencer Marketing: 0 in FY25, targeting 5-6 Cr in FY26
growth verticals / optionality: Exclusion server distribution (India-China trade normalization could unlock 5-10x revenue); AI product suite (15 products in pipeline, 7-8 launched); e-commerce portal for spare parts (future monetization); geographic expansion to 10 cities (Ahmedabad, Chennai, Kolkata, Noida) enabling local service delivery
margins & cost dynamics: Hardware AMC: 25-30% EBITDA; Software/Products: 40-45% EBITDA; Influencer Marketing: 35-40% EBITDA; Exclusion Server: 10-15% EBITDA; overall PAT margin target 20% — low-margin Exclusion sales will pressure overall margin but boost top-line credibility for tenders
capex / expansion: No major capex planned beyond inventory build-up for AMC (spare parts) and branch office rentals. Office purchase (Rupa Solitaire) already completed in FY25.
capital allocation: Prioritizing inventory for AMC, expanding digital sales team (Hyderabad, Noida, Chennai), funding R&D for AI products, and maintaining liquidity for Exclusion server inventory. No dividend or buyback announced.
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration risk (top 5 clients ~25-30% revenue); receivables rising to 6.5 Cr (110+ days); Exclusion server revenue delayed due to India-China trade tensions; margin compression from low-margin hardware sales; execution risk in scaling 10x enterprise digital business
management quality / tone: Confident, aggressive, and transparent — management openly acknowledges low-margin business for top-line growth, highlights strategic separation of digital arm, and sets bold FY26 targets with clear order book backing. Tone is entrepreneurial, not corporate.
non-obvious takeaways: The 45 Cr order is not just a project — it’s a template for bundled telecom contracts (software + hardware + 10-year AMC + managed services) that Olatech can replicate; influencer marketing is not just a service but a productized platform with IP (Earnin.me) and regional sales teams; Exclusion server distribution is a hidden lever — if India-China trade eases, this could become a 50 Cr+ business with minimal capex

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.
